🔥 I’ve completed my second prototype of a fan-laced crochet corset. This time, I incorporated synthetic whalebone as a type of corset boning, which is better than the spiral steel boning I used in my first version. It looks more structured than my initial attempt. The boning is securely stitched underneath the corset using a boning tunnel/casing. I used a sturdy wax cord that can withstand pulling for the lacing. I paired it with my freehand crocheted bustier top. This corset is for aesthetic purposes only and is a statement piece in your wardrobe. It will not function as a traditional corset because it is a crocheted version with added structure.  The crochet pattern will be available for purchase soon! It is currently in the testing phase. Ch 17 (or another odd # of your choosing), hold your place, ch5 more, dc into the 17th chain that you’re holding (or whatever odd # you chose), ch1, skip a chain and dc into the 2nd stitch, ch1, skip a chain and dc into the second stitch. Continue till the end. Ch1 and turn, dc into the first stitch. Ch1, skip the space & dc into the next stitch. Ch1, skip the space & dc into the next stitch. Continue till the end. Repeat this row until desired length.   #crochetscarf #crochetheadband #crochettutorial #crochet #freecrochetpattern

Alexandria Masse is a Canadian textile artist making a powerful statement about reproductive rights. She’s creating the Birth Control Tapestry, a massive project where she crochets her birth control info sheet word for word. Each stitch is done during her menstruation week, making the work deeply personal and tied to her own body. Since starting in 2025, she has poured months of dedication into this piece, using kilometers of yarn to build a tapestry already larger than herself. The artwork sparks conversations about bodily autonomy, women’s rights, and healthcare access, turning knowledge into a tangible, immersive experience. Alexandria hopes to display the finished tapestry in a museum or gallery, so visitors can see the full scale and feel the history and struggles woven into every stitch. Her project blends artistry, activism, and education, showing how creativity can make a real difference.
